checkpoints.title: Protect data in transit and at rest separately
checkpoints.prompt: A developer stores invoices sent from users’ browsers to an order API in S3. The organization requires HTTPS for communication and SSE-KMS using a specified KMS key for storage. Choose one way to verify both requirements.

choices.text: Separately verify HTTPS across the entire path and the SSE-KMS configuration and KMS key applied to the object in S3.
choices.explanation: This verifies the requirements for encrypting communications and the storage destination’s encryption method and key separately.

choices.text: Verify only that HTTPS is used between the browser and the order API.
choices.explanation: This does not verify the path from the API to S3 or the specified-key requirement for data at rest.

choices.text: Do not verify the KMS key used because S3 default encryption protects new objects.
choices.explanation: S3 default SSE-S3 encryption alone may not satisfy the requirement to use the KMS key specified by the organization.

choices.text: Verify only that the S3 object uses SSE-KMS.
choices.explanation: This does not verify the specified key or HTTPS for the communication path.

learning.reason: Communication and storage are separate boundaries.
learning.concept: Data in transit and at rest

checkpoints.title: Verify the KMS key and access permissions separately
checkpoints.prompt: When an operations engineer tries to read an S3 object encrypted with SSE-KMS from an application, access is denied. Choose one way to isolate the cause.

choices.text: Verify only whether the key ARN is known.
choices.explanation: Identification information is not permission.

choices.text: Grant kms:Decrypt to everyone.
choices.explanation: This grants excessive permissions.

choices.text: Verify the read permission for the S3 object and the decrypt permission allowed by the KMS key policy or IAM policy.
choices.explanation: This verifies the authorization boundaries for the data and the key.

choices.text: Delete and recreate the bucket.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve the cause and risks data loss.

learning.reason: This verifies the authorization boundaries for the data and the key.

checkpoints.title: Verify backup success and restorability separately
checkpoints.prompt: A database administrator confirmed that the backup was created successfully. It has not been verified whether order processing can resume within the recovery time objective (RTO). Choose one verification to perform next.

choices.text: Treat the success notification as an audit trail and finish.
choices.explanation: This does not demonstrate restorability.

choices.text: Restore to an isolated destination and record the elapsed time, integrity, and application connectivity.
choices.explanation: This allows comparison of the objective with the measured result.

choices.text: Delete the production data and try a restore.
choices.explanation: This is not a safe test.

choices.text: Change the RTO to match the measured result.
choices.explanation: The measurement must come first.

learning.reason: This allows comparison of the objective with the measured result.

checkpoints.title: Separate secret storage, retrieval, and display
checkpoints.prompt: An operations administrator found a token for an external API used by an order-processing application in the source code and error logs. Choose one action to improve secret management.

choices.text: Make the logs public to everyone for monitoring
choices.explanation: This broadens the scope of the leak.

choices.text: Move it to another source file
choices.explanation: The plaintext problem remains.

choices.text: Make the execution role an administrator
choices.explanation: This does not solve the storage and display problems.

choices.text: Move it to Secrets Manager, restrict who can retrieve it, and remove the value from the logs
choices.explanation: This separates storage, retrieval, and display.

learning.reason: This separates storage, retrieval, and display.

choices.text: Use HTTPS/TLS
choices.explanation: HTTPS/TLS protects data in transit.

choices.text: Enable only S3 encryption at rest
choices.explanation: Encrypting only the storage destination does not protect the path to the API.

choices.text: Log the name of the KMS key
choices.explanation: Displaying key information does not encrypt communications.

finalQuestions.prompt: A web administrator wants to prevent third parties on the communication path from reading customer information when it is sent from a browser to an order API. Select one setting that directly addresses this requirement.
finalQuestions.title: Protection in Transit

choices.text: If you confirm that HTTPS is being used, you can determine that the invoice was stored with the specified KMS key.
choices.explanation: HTTPS protects communications. You must separately verify the encryption method and key for the object stored in S3.

choices.text: Verify that the encryption method for the stored invoice is SSE-KMS and that the key is the one specified by the organization.
choices.explanation: This verifies whether the stored object meets the data protection requirements.

choices.text: Verify that the execution role used by the application for writing has permission to use the target KMS key.
choices.explanation: In addition to permissions allowing writes to S3, verify the key-use permissions required for SSE-KMS.

finalQuestions.prompt: A web administrator stores invoices received over HTTPS in S3. The organization requires the stored invoices to use a specified KMS key. Select the one incorrect judgment when verifying this requirement.
finalQuestions.title: Protection at Rest

choices.text: Check TLS from the browser to the API
choices.explanation: This protects communication from the user to the API.

choices.text: Do not check the path from the API to S3
choices.explanation: Communication from the API to the storage destination is also protected.

choices.text: Check the storage encryption and the principal that uses the key
choices.explanation: Check the encryption at rest and the permissions to use the key.

finalQuestions.prompt: Customer information is stored in S3 through an API from a browser. Select two correct objects to check for protection.
finalQuestions.title: Organizing Protection Boundaries

choices.text: S3 read permissions and KMS key decrypt permissions
choices.explanation: The data and the key are separate authorization boundaries.

choices.text: Only the name of the KMS key
choices.explanation: Identification information is not permission to use the key.

choices.text: Change the execution role's trust policy to allow principals from all AWS accounts as trusted entities.
choices.explanation: Expanding the trusted entities does not verify the permissions required for S3 or KMS. It unnecessarily broadens who can assume the role.

finalQuestions.prompt: When the order API attempts to read an S3 object, AccessDenied is returned. The object is encrypted with SSE-KMS. Select two items that are incorrect as investigations or responses to the cause.
finalQuestions.title: KMS Access Permissions

choices.text: Decryption is always possible with only an IAM policy
choices.explanation: The key policy cannot be ignored.

choices.text: Check the key policy, IAM policy, and, if necessary, grants together
choices.explanation: KMS usage permissions are determined by a combination of authorization elements.

choices.text: If the configuration does not use grants, verify that grants are unnecessary
choices.explanation: Even when grants are not used, check the combination of the key policy and IAM policy.

finalQuestions.prompt: We allowed kms:Decrypt for an IAM role, but the key policy for the target KMS key does not allow the use of IAM policies. Select one incorrect check.
finalQuestions.title: KMS Authorization

choices.text: Allow only the necessary operations to the required principals that need to use the target key
choices.explanation: This limits the target, principals, and operations.

choices.text: Allow kms:* for all roles
choices.explanation: This expands permissions to include unnecessary administrative and decryption permissions.

choices.text: Use the key policy to verify that the principal can use the target key
choices.explanation: The key policy is also an element of KMS authorization.

finalQuestions.prompt: The order application retrieves only database credentials from AWS Secrets Manager. The secret is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key. Select two appropriate actions when allowing the application to decrypt it.

source.label: AWS KMS key access and permissions

finalQuestions.title: Least privilege

choices.text: Save the success notification and stop.
choices.explanation: Successful creation alone does not demonstrate usability.

choices.text: Unconditionally overwrite-restore to the production database.
choices.explanation: This is not a safe testing procedure.

choices.text: Restore to an isolated destination and verify integrity and application connectivity.
choices.explanation: You can verify this through an actual restore and usability check.

finalQuestions.prompt: The AWS Backup job succeeded. Select two incorrect next steps for verifying recoverability.
finalQuestions.title: Restore Testing

choices.text: Measure the recovery time and compare it with the RTO
choices.explanation: This allows the required time to be measured in practice.

choices.text: Do not check the number of orders after restoration
choices.explanation: This makes it impossible to determine consistency.

choices.text: Check the recovery point and compare it with the RPO
choices.explanation: This verifies how far the recovery progressed.

choices.text: Select and test an isolated restoration target
choices.explanation: Prepare a restoration target that does not affect production first.

finalQuestions.prompt: The operations team for the order service verifies whether it can restore order data from a database backup in preparation for a failure. There are objectives for recovery time and the amount of data that may be lost. Select one procedure that is incorrect for the verification.
finalQuestions.title: Recovery objectives

choices.text: Measure the time required to restore from the backup.
choices.explanation: The time required for restoration is part of the recovery time used for comparison with the objective.

choices.text: Connect to the restoration target from the application and verify the integrity of the order data.
choices.explanation: After the restoration completes, also verify that the application can use the data.

choices.text: A restoration test is an operation that deletes the backup
choices.explanation: Restore to an isolated target and verify it.

finalQuestions.prompt: The operations team restores a backup of the order database to another database and determines whether the order service can be restarted during a failure. Select two checks needed for that determination.
finalQuestions.title: Backup and restoration

choices.text: The token is stored in Secrets Manager, and the order application retrieves it using an execution role.
choices.explanation: This separates the application code from the secret and allows the retrieval scope to be controlled through the execution role.

choices.text: The token is recorded as a plaintext constant in the source code and remains in the repository's change history.
choices.explanation: The secret can be read from the history. Consider it compromised, revoke or reissue it, and move to a method that does not record it in the code.

choices.text: When recording API errors in logs, the field that would record the token itself is omitted.
choices.explanation: This preserves the records needed for troubleshooting while reducing the paths through which the token could leak from the logs.

finalQuestions.prompt: An operations engineer is reviewing an order application that uses a token for an external API. Select one area that should be prioritized for remediation to manage the token securely.
finalQuestions.title: Storing Secrets

choices.text: Allow retrieval of only secret-a
choices.explanation: This limits the target secret.

choices.text: Allow retrieval of all secrets
choices.explanation: This exposes unnecessary secrets.

choices.text: Always write retrieved values to the logs
choices.explanation: The logs become a path for leakage.

finalQuestions.prompt: A developer gives the order application's execution role only the minimum permissions required for operations. The only secret the application needs to read is secret-a. Select one permission that should be granted.
finalQuestions.title: Secret Retrieval Permissions

choices.text: Verify that the application can connect using the new value
choices.explanation: This verifies the consumer after the update.

choices.text: Output the old value to an incident log for comparison
choices.explanation: The old value is also a secret and must not be output.

choices.text: Change the execution role to an administrator role
choices.explanation: Excessive permissions are unnecessary.

choices.text: Verify that the value does not appear in logs or error responses
choices.explanation: This prevents leakage through display paths.

finalQuestions.prompt: A person responsible for the order application verifies its behavior after rotating database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Select two methods that are incorrect for verification.
finalQuestions.title: Secret Rotation

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.text: Distinguish between encryption in transit and at rest, KMS authorization, restoration testing, and the retrieval and display of secrets.

blocks.label: Learning objective
blocks.text: Determine from specific conditions the protection scenario, the entity using the key, recoverability, and the exposure path for secrets.

blocks.label: Learning objective
blocks.text: Distinguish the protection boundaries for data in transit and at rest, and verify S3 encryption settings.

blocks.label: Learning objective
blocks.text: Explain the relationship between a KMS key policy, IAM policy, grant, and the principal that performs decryption.

blocks.label: Learning objective
blocks.text: Separate backup success from recoverability, and verify RTO/RPO through an actual restoration.

blocks.label: Learning objective
blocks.text: Separate secrets from code and logs, and minimize permissions to retrieve the target secret.

blocks.label: Protect data in transit and at rest separately
blocks.text: Data moving from the browser to the API and from the API to the storage destination is in transit. HTTPS protects HTTP with TLS, but protecting the communication path and protecting the storage destination are separate concerns.

blocks.label: Protect data in transit and at rest separately
blocks.text: Objects newly uploaded to Amazon S3 are encrypted at rest. The standard method is SSE-S3, which uses keys managed by S3. When a requirement specifies using a KMS key, verify both the object's encryption method and that the execution role has permission to use that key.

blocks.label: Protect data in transit and at rest separately
blocks.text: In a design review, list the path, storage location, and accessing principal separately. Do not consider the review complete after checking only data in transit or only data at rest.

steps.label: Protect data in transit and at rest separately

blocks.label: Scenario
blocks.text: A customer uploads an invoice from a web interface, and the API stores it in S3.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Use HTTPS from the browser to the API.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Verify the path from the API to S3 and S3's default encryption.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: If SSE-KMS is required, verify the encryption method for the actual object, the specified KMS key, and the permissions that allow the application to use that key.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can verify separate protection boundaries for data in transit, data at rest, and key usage.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: Uploading over HTTPS means that the organization-designated KMS key is also used for files stored in S3.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: HTTPS protects the network path. For objects stored in S3, verify the encryption method and KMS key in the S3 configuration or in the specification made when writing the object.

blocks.label: Takeaway
blocks.text: TLS protects data in transit.

blocks.label: Takeaway
blocks.text: Verify encryption at rest in the storage service.

blocks.label: Takeaway
blocks.text: Verify the encryption method and key usage permissions separately.

blocks.label: Verify KMS keys and usage permissions separately
blocks.text: AWS KMS manages encryption keys. Merely specifying a key does not mean that arbitrary principals can perform encryption operations.

blocks.label: Verify KMS keys and usage permissions separately
blocks.text: Whether KMS can be used is determined by the combination of the key policy, IAM policy, and grant. Even if IAM allows it, the permission is not effective unless the key policy permits that configuration.

blocks.label: Verify KMS keys and usage permissions separately
blocks.text: During troubleshooting, separate the permission to read the target data from the permission to decrypt it with the encryption key. Allow only the required principals and operations.

steps.label: Verify KMS keys and usage permissions separately

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The application cannot read an S3 object encrypted with SSE-KMS.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Identify the target object and the execution role.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Check the S3 read permission.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Check the decryption permission in the KMS key policy and IAM policy.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can troubleshoot the denial on the S3 side separately from the denial on the KMS side.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: Allowing kms:Decrypt in an IAM policy lets you decrypt with any KMS key.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: The target key’s key policy and grant are also evaluated. Check the permission for both the key and the principal.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: The existence of a key does not grant permission to use it.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: Check the key policy, IAM policy, and grant for the target key and principal.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: Allow decryption operations only for the principals that need them.

blocks.label: Verify backup success and restorability separately
blocks.text: A successful backup job shows that recovery data was created, but it does not prove that you can restore the required state or that the application can be used.

blocks.label: Verify backup success and restorability separately
blocks.text: Define how to verify the recovery point, restore destination, RTO, RPO, data integrity, and application connectivity. Perform an actual restore in an isolated environment and evaluate it, as with AWS Backup restore testing.

blocks.label: Verify backup success and restorability separately
blocks.text: A restore test does not overwrite production. Record the time required, omissions, and reconnection procedure, then update the difference between the plan and the measured results.

steps.label: Verify backup success and restorability separately

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The overnight backup of the orders database succeeds, but the restoration procedure has not been tested.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Choose a recovery point and an isolated restoration target.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Restore the database and verify its integrity and application connectivity.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Record the duration and results by comparing them with the RTO/RPO.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can verify whether the system can be returned to an available state within the required time.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: A backup success notification means that the recovery plan is complete.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: Actually verify the restoration procedure, post-restoration integrity, application connectivity, and duration.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: Backup and restore validation are separate tasks.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: Determine the restore destination and validation criteria first.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: Perform restore testing in an isolated environment and compare the results with the RTO/RPO.

blocks.label: Separate the storage, retrieval, and display of secrets
blocks.text: Passwords, API keys, and tokens are secrets. Placing them in plaintext in source code, configuration files, chats, or logs increases the number of viewers and replication locations.

blocks.label: Separate the storage, retrieval, and display of secrets
blocks.text: Store them in AWS Secrets Manager, and have the application retrieve only the secrets it needs using its execution role. Preparing a storage location does not provide protection if retrieval permissions are too broad.

blocks.label: Separate the storage, retrieval, and display of secrets
blocks.text: Do not output values in logs or error responses, limit access to the relevant secrets, and confirm that dependent applications can keep up after an update.

steps.label: Separate the storage, retrieval, and display of secrets

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The application uses an external API token and records request information in logs when a failure occurs.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Register the token in Secrets Manager and remove it from the code.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Allow the execution role to retrieve only the target secret.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Verify that values do not appear in logs or error displays.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: Separating the storage location, retrieval principal, and display path helps limit the scope of a leak.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: It is safe to expose secrets in logs if they are environment variables.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: Environment variables are also runtime secrets. Do not expose their values in logs or errors, and limit who can retrieve them.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: Separate secrets from code and logs.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: Minimize permissions to retrieve the target secret.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: Confirm that the value is not displayed or collected even after rotation.
